predecessors.name: Thebes and the Theban hegemony
predecessors.text: the Boeotian cities, which Thebes kept when the hegemony ended

successors.name: Greek city-states (independent poleis)
successors.text: Philip 'did not, however, dissolve the Boeotian Confederacy'; Thebes surrendered and received a Macedonian garrison

ledger.x: 361: after Mantinea Thebes falls back on the Boeotian League.
356: Phocis seizes Delphi and the Third Sacred War begins.
347: Phocian garrisons hold the Boeotian cities of Orchomenus, Coronea and Corsiae.
346: Philip gives the captured Boeotian cities back to Thebes.
346: Phocis surrenders and the Third Sacred War ends.
338: Philip wins at Chaeronea and Thebes surrenders.

wars.name: Third Sacred War
wars.outcome: Amphictyonic League victory: Phocis was expelled from the Amphictyonic council and its cities ordered destroyed, but it kept its land; Philip restored the Boeotian cities Phocis had captured and Macedon took Phocis's two votes.

wars.name: Battle of Chaeronea (338 BC)
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory; Thebes surrendered and took a Macedonian garrison, the Second Athenian League was dissolved and the League of Corinth followed in the latter half of 337.

certainty.note: The Boeotian frontier is not given by any page opened; the Phocian frontier is approximate and Philip's settlement of 346 restored cities, not a surveyed line.
